ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Real Decreto-ley 7/2019 and Ley 13/2022; and Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010, as amended by Real Decreto 959/2021, de 2 de noviembre. The UBO disclosure obligation is implemented through Articles 3, 4, 14 and 37 of Ley 10/2010 and Articles 9 to 12 of Real Decreto 304/2014, and is recorded through the Registro Mercantil system and notarial protocols.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social (Negative Name Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original administrative certificate for domestic use; no apostille required unless subsequently produced abroad, in which case Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Justice is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Escritura Pública de Constitución y Estatutos Sociales (Notarial Public Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial protocol attestation; Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Justice is required only if the deed is to be used in another Hague States jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Corporate Extract of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign companies registry or equivalent competent authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; for non-Hague Convention countries, Spanish consular legalization at the Spanish Embassy or Consulate of that jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder) granted by foreign corporate shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner to the Spanish incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the jurisdiction of each foreign UBO or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Spanish Consular Legalization, accompanied by sworn translation into Spanish by a certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport or national identity document and proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification, then Hague Apostille or Spanish Consular Legalization where required by the Spanish notary or AML compliance officer

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC); applicable Articles 4 (minimum capital), 17 (registered office), 20-22 (public deed and bylaws), 30-33 (inscription and legal personality), 59-72 (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada regime); supplemented by Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil), Articles 175-180.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry – name reservation) and Registro Mercantil Provincial del domicilio social (Provincial Commercial Registry – incorporation inscription); under the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública, Ministerio de Justicia.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (public incorporation deed) executed before a Spanish notary and submitted to the Provincial Mercantile Registry for mandatory inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) requires minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at incorporation. The funds must be deposited in a Spanish bank account opened in the company's name (certificado de depósito bancario) and blocked until registration, or delivered directly to the notary in escrow. In-kind contributions require an independent expert valuation report under LSC Article 67.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION. The Sole Founding Shareholder of [COMPANY NAME], S.L., resolves as follows: (1) Share Subscription: approve the subscription, by the founding shareholder, of the entire share capital of EUR 3,000, divided into 3,000 participations of EUR 1.00 each, and acknowledge the blocked bank certificate evidencing full payment. (2) Registered Office: adopt as the statutory registered office and effective management center the premises at [ADDRESS], [CITY], Spain, within the jurisdiction of the [CITY] Mercantile Registry. (3) Officers: appoint [NAME] as Sole Administrator and [NAME] as Non-Member Secretary, confirming the Administrator's powers, including incorporation acts. Executed at [CITY], [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Name Certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, online via www.rmc.es
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the online application for certification that the proposed corporate name has no prior registration. Submit up to three alternative names in order of preference, pay the official fee via bank transfer or TPV, and download the electronic certificate once approved. The certificate is valid for three months and must be attached to the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE of the founding shareholder
List of three proposed corporate names in order of preference
Payment receipt of the official fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is refused due to identity with an existing company, submit the next alternative name; if all names are rejected, file a fresh application with new name proposals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Spanish Bank Account and Deposit Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution regulated by Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an account in the name of the company 'in formation' (e.g., '[COMPANY NAME], S.L. en constitución') presenting the notarial draft bylaws and name certificate. Deposit EUR 3,000 as fully paid share capital. Obtain an official bank certificate (certificado de depósito bancario) confirming the deposit and the blocking of funds until the Mercantile Registry inscription.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE of the founding shareholder and ultimate beneficial owners
Anti-money laundering declaration and source-of-funds information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the selected bank rejects the onboarding file, open the account at an alternative Spanish bank; alternatively, the capital may be delivered to the notary as a public deposit and referenced in the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Public Incorporation Deed before a Spanish Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the jurisdiction of the registered office (Colegio de Notarios)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver to the notary the name certificate, bank certificate, draft bylaws, and identification documents. The notary verifies legal capacity and compliance with LSC Articles 20-22, drafts the escritura pública, and schedules a signing appointment. All founding shareholders must sign personally or by legal representative. The notary issues certified first copies for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Tax identification details of legal-entity shareholders, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution due to defective clauses, amend the bylaws by supplementary statement and re-notarize; if the notary lacks capacity or availability, select another notary in the same jurisdiction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – local tax office of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the deed, submit Form 036 (declaración censal) together with a notarized copy of the incorporation deed to obtain a provisional NIF (CIF provisional) starting with 'J' before the company is registered in the Mercantile Registry. Attach the identification of the designated legal representative.
required_dossiers: First copy or certified copy of the public incorporation deed
NIE and passport of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT issues a requirement for missing documents, supply the additional evidence within 10 business days; verify the form's box declarations before filing to avoid procedural rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscribe the Company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original notarial deed, provisional NIF certificate, and a filing form to the provincial registry. The registrar performs a legal qualification review (calificación) of the deed and bylaws. Upon approval, the entry is made, and certified copies (certificación de inscripción) are issued; legal personality is acquired on inscription per LSC Article 33.
required_dossiers: Original first copy of the public incorporation deed
Proof of payment of registry fees
Power of attorney if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar suspends or denies inscription, rectify the defective clauses through a new notarial deed or a supplementary resolution and resubmit; appeal the qualification decision through the Civil and Commercial Registry Directorate (DGSJFP) if the defect is unwarranted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive NIF and Complete Post-Registration Formalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT; Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS); notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Mercantile Registry inscription, submit Form 036 again to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF. Register the company with TGSS for employer social security obligations, execute the legalization of corporate books (books of participations, minutes, and accounting) at the Mercantile Registry, and apply for an electronic certificate for digital tax filing and e-invoicing.
required_dossiers: Certification of registration from the Mercantile Registry
Completed social security employer registration form (modelo TA-6 or telematic equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF conversion is delayed, request a certificate of registered status from the Mercantile Registry and present it to AEAT; if corporate book legalization is rejected, correct formal defects and resubmit within the statutory period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Industria, Economía y Empleo of the respective Autonomous Community (e.g., Comunidad de Madrid) and the municipal Ayuntamiento for activity and opening licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Actividad y Apertura (Municipal Activity and Opening License) or, for low-risk premises, Declaración Responsable under Ley 12/2012 de dinamización de la actividad comercial; a separate warehouse license is only required if the company operates storage facilities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) and the competent environmental agency of the Autonomous Community.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Pure online resale of furniture is generally exempt from EIA. If warehousing/logistics premises exceed the thresholds of Annex II of Ley 21/2013, a simplified environmental registration or full EIA may be required; otherwise only municipal environmental integration applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Real Decreto 102/2011 for urban wastewater discharges into municipal sewers where applicable; no VOC-emitting varnishing or finishing processes in pure resale; packaging and packaging waste obligations under Ley 7/2022 and Real Decreto 1055/2022; waste transfer documents for disposal of damaged or returned furniture.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for occupied premises per CTE DB-SI and Real Decreto 2267/2004 for storage areas, issued with municipal fire inspection; structural load inspection and building occupancy certificate (licencia de primera ocupación) or technical inspection report (ITE) for older premises; workplace occupational risk prevention evaluation under Ley 31/1995 and Real Decreto 486/1997 for warehouse and logistics operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), through the AEAT Sede Electrónica tax portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains its Spanish tax identification number (NIF) by filing Modelo 036 with the AEAT before commencing business activities, acquiring assets, hiring employees, or entering into taxable transactions. The NIF is generally the entity's corporate tax and VAT identification number; for EU VAT transactions it is used with the ES prefix. Incorporation data are normally transmitted to the AEAT through the Commercial Registry and notarial process, but the company remains responsible for confirming activation and registered activities. A foreign shareholder or foreign entity requiring a Spanish tax identifier applies for a NIF/NIE, as applicable, using Modelo 036 or the applicable AEAT procedure. Supporting documents may include the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, proof of authority, identification of directors or representatives, Spanish tax representative details where required, and a power of attorney. Foreign public documents generally require apostille or legalization and an official Spanish translation. Nonresident entities registering for Spanish VAT must file Modelo 036, identify the relevant economic activities and VAT obligations, and obtain or validate an ES-prefixed VAT number. Registration in the Register of Intra-Community Operators (ROI) is separately requested through Modelo 036 and is subject to AEAT approval.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal taxpayer; Spain has no general United States-style check-the-box election. Available elective or regime-based mechanisms may include the tax consolidation regime for qualifying corporate groups, the special regime for mergers, demergers and other qualifying reorganizations, the cash-accounting special VAT regime where eligibility conditions are satisfied, the monthly VAT refund regime (REDEME), and special regimes for qualifying holding, investment, or internationally oriented activities. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Corporate Income Tax Law restrict deductions, exempt income, or impose inclusion where arrangements produce deduction or non-inclusion, double deduction, or imported mismatch outcomes. Elections and applications generally require statutory deadlines, eligibility conditions, and formal notification to the AEAT.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Spanish Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), harmonized with the EU VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies for Spanish VAT registration. A person or entity carrying out an economic activity independently in Spain must generally register before commencing taxable activities, irrespective of turnover. The Spanish domestic registration obligation is distinct from the EU distance-selling threshold of EUR 10,000 for certain intra-EU consumer transactions, which may be managed through the Union One Stop Shop (OSS). Imports, intra-Community acquisitions, local supplies, and marketplace or warehouse activities may create additional registration obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spanish VAT invoices must satisfy statutory content, integrity, authenticity, legibility, numbering, date, supplier and customer identification, VAT rate, taxable base, VAT amount, and transaction-description requirements. Electronic invoices are permitted when recipient acceptance and authenticity and integrity controls are satisfied. The Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system requires qualifying taxpayers, including taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups, and certain entities that elect into the system, to transmit specified invoice-record data electronically to the AEAT, generally within four calendar days, subject to statutory exclusions and special timing rules. Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time clearance requirement for every invoice. Law 18/2022 establishes a future business-to-business electronic invoicing framework, with implementation dependent on regulatory development and phased effective dates; businesses must monitor the applicable commencement date for their size and turnover category. The VERI*FACTU compliant billing-system framework requires integrity, traceability, anti-tampering controls, event records, and, where applicable, transmission of invoice records to the AEAT. Digital invoicing, SII, and customs electronic declarations are separate compliance systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Spanish VAT does not generally label exports as zero-rated supplies; qualifying exports of goods to destinations outside the EU are VAT-exempt with the right to deduct input VAT. The supplier must establish that the goods leave the EU customs territory and that the transaction is supplied by, or on behalf of, the Spanish supplier or qualifies under the applicable export arrangement. Core evidence includes a valid commercial invoice, export customs declaration with the supplier's export status, transport or shipping evidence, proof of exit or equivalent customs confirmation, and matching accounting and payment records. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct where the customer is identified for VAT in another EU Member State, the goods are dispatched or transported from Spain to that Member State, and the supplier holds valid transport and customer-identification evidence and correctly reports the transaction. Services are generally taxed according to place-of-supply rules rather than an export zero-rating rule. Business-to-business services supplied to a customer established outside Spain may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT where the general place-of-supply rule applies, subject to special rules for immovable property, transport, events, electronically supplied services, financial services, and other categories. Input VAT refunds may be claimed through the periodic VAT return, the REDEME monthly refund system, or applicable nonestablished-business refund procedures, subject to documentary and procedural conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the Spanish supplier, customer, goods, value, and VAT treatment
Electronic export customs declaration, normally containing the applicable customs procedure and exporter's EORI identification
Customs exit confirmation or other legally accepted evidence that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Bill of lading, sea waybill, air waybill, CMR consignment note, courier record, or equivalent transport document
Packing list and shipment details sufficient to reconcile the goods with the invoice and customs declaration
Proof of delivery or destination evidence where relevant to the transport chain
Customer order, sales contract, warehouse release record, and accounting records supporting the transaction
Payment evidence and bank records; an inward-remittance certificate is not generally a statutory condition for Spanish export VAT exemption
For intra-Community supplies: customer's valid EU VAT number, transport evidence to another Member State, and required recapitulative statement reporting
For VAT refunds: valid purchase invoices, import VAT documents where applicable, customs payment evidence, and VAT return or refund-claim records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.mandatory_fx_repatriation_deadline_days: Not applicable. Spain does not impose a general 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation requirement as a condition for export VAT exemption or input VAT recovery. Export proceeds may remain abroad subject to ordinary banking, anti-money-laundering, accounting, transfer-pricing, customs, and corporate-tax requirements. Sector-specific financing, subsidy, sanctions, or contractual rules may impose separate reporting or repatriation obligations.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEAT may deny the VAT exemption or input VAT refund, assess the unpaid VAT retrospectively, charge late-payment interest, and impose penalties where export departure, transport, customer VAT status, invoicing, or reporting is inadequately substantiated. Incorrectly exempt domestic supplies may be reassessed at the applicable VAT rate, with statutory interest and penalties. Penalties depend on the infringement and may include proportional penalties for failure to charge or pay VAT, failure to maintain or provide records, inaccurate returns, fraudulent conduct, obstruction, or use of falsified documents; aggravated cases may attract higher penalties and criminal tax consequences where statutory criminal thresholds and intent requirements are met. The AEAT may also recover unduly refunded or deducted input VAT, apply joint-liability or successor-liability rules in qualifying circumstances, and examine connected-party pricing, customs valuation, fulfillment-center records, and marketplace data. Fraudulent customs or VAT documentation may additionally trigger customs debt, import or export sanctions, seizure measures, and criminal investigation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks and the Eurosystem; external transactions and balance-of-payments reporting are administered jointly with the Spanish Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation (Ministerio de Asuntos Económicos y Transformación Digital) and the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOM) for capital movement statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain does not maintain a domestic foreign-exchange-control law that restricts convertibility. The euro is fully convertible, and Spain applies the EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital. Current-account payments (trade in goods, services, licenses, salaries) are free of prior authorisation, and capital-account operations (equity injection, loan disbursements, dividend repatriation, liquidation proceeds) are likewise unrestricted for EU residents and non-EU investors subject only to statistical reporting through the Banco de España 'Survey of Foreign Transactions' system. Profit remittance to non-residents is not administratively gated; however, corporate-law restrictions for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) require that distributable reserves exist and that the shareholders' meeting approves a dividend, and cross-border dividend payments are generally subject to Spanish withholding tax of 19% unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation in Spain or under EU law to surrender export proceeds to the central bank or a local banking system, and no mandatory conversion ratio applies. Exporters may freely retain foreign currency in non-resident or offshore accounts, or convert into euro at the commercial bank's market rate. Export invoices must be correctly documented in the supporting trade file for VAT, customs, and balance-of-payments reporting, but the timing of repatriation is unregulated; full autonomy is granted to the exporter as long as the underlying commercial transaction is genuine and complies with EU customs and cash-control regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Depósito/Reserva) and Operational Treasury Account
Capital Escrow Account and Current Account with multibank FX access
Operational Account in EUR and USD, with trade-finance and LC facilities
Operational Account and Cross-Border Collection Account
Corporate Account with dedicated commercial-client treasury desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-to-High only for euro-denominated transactional sweep accounts, but Low for core treasury concentration. A fully licensed EU e-money institution (EMI) passported into Spain under Directive 2009/110/EC can, in principle, provide payment accounts and acquire FX for trade settlements without a full banking license. However, an offshore digital EMI that is not licensed or passported in Spain cannot lawfully maintain a Spanish IBAN or collect client funds as a deposit-taking institution, and the SL must ensure that any non-bank payment institution holds funds in segregated accounts at an EU credit institution. For oversized home-furniture e-commerce, an EMI alone is not advisable because commercial letters of credit, large USD correspondents, and high-volume Marketplace payouts require banking-grade clearance and treasury buffers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish AML law (Ley 10/2010 and subsequent regulations) does not expressly mandate a physical appearance for a corporate account opening, but internal risk policies of the major Spanish banks overwhelmingly require a face-to-face interview for foreign-shareholder corporate vehicles. In practice, at least one director or a designated authorised representative with a duly notarised and apostilled power of attorney must appear before the branch in Spain to sign the account-opening documents and complete enhanced due diligence. Remote onboarding is available only for low-risk EU-domiciled companies with a Spanish legal representative and a prior commercial relationship; for an SL with non-resident shareholders, a remote video interview may be accepted by some banks, but only if the original corporate documents, passport copies, and proof of address are certified by an apostilled notary and forwarded through a recognised Spanish notary or registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity due to non-resident shareholders and overseas holding layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Spanish public registry certificate (certificación literal del Registro Mercantil), articles of association showing the share capital as filed, a current beneficial-ownership register (Libro de Registro de Titularidades Reales) signed by the secretary, personal identification and passports of all shareholders holding more than 25%, and a notarially drawn shareholder-control diagram with UBO declaration on Spanish tax Form 232 if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth for the initial capital contribution coming from outside the EU
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements for the immediately preceding six months from the remitting institution, evidence of tax domicile of the remitting entity, signed declaration on Form S1 / statement of sources of wealth, commercial contracts or sale records proving the origin of funds, and an identifiable link to the online retail furniture business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Geography mismatch between the bank's location, the company's commercial counterparties, and oversized goods logistics in Latin America
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Warehouse and distribution contracts with third-party logistics providers, transport insurance policies, customs representation agreements, purchase orders from Latin American distributors, and evidence of physical shipping arrangements proving the commercial rationale for cross-border payment flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high transaction velocity with Buy-Now-Pay-Later clearing flows and potentially low average ticket but high aggregate volume
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pro-forma cash-flow forecast, marketplace-clearing agreements with Stripe and Affirm BNPL, customer refund policy, anti-fraud and chargeback monitoring procedures, and a written AML-compliant business plan approved by the compliance officer of the SL.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections from a non-resident parent into the Spanish SL are executed by a SWIFT MT103 (ISO 20022 pacs.008 for euro) to the SL's operational account at the Spanish bank. The wire must include the correct beneficiary (SL with complete address and account IBAN), a transparent reference such as 'Capital Contribution under Spanish Limited Liability Law', and a Balance-of-Payments purpose code identifying direct investment equity (commonly reported by the beneficiary bank to the Banco de España as code C2 or B06 depending on the bank's statistical reporting matrix). The SL must verify the remitter's bank credentials and any encrypted message from the sending institution; for amounts above EUR 10,000 an original capital-movement statistical declaration (Declaración de Inversiones Exteriores) must be filed post-transaction. Spanish banks may request the shareholders' meeting resolution approving the capital increase and proof of the mirror entries in the parent's accounting records before releasing funds for operating purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements for outbound trade settlements in oversized furniture should be cleared through (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments in USD or EUR; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) for ordinary euro payments to EU counterparties; and (iii) commercial letters of credit under UCP600 (MT700 and MT707 amendments) for high-value Latin American distribution contracts, particularly where a bank confirming the credit in the buyer's country is involved. USD-denominated payments are cleared through the Spanish bank's correspondent network with JP Morgan, Citibank, or Bank of New York Mellon, in which case the beneficiary must be clearly annotated with the invoice and purchase-order numbers to avoid trade-finance rejection. Spain's national real-time clearing circuit is not applicable to cross-border trade; commercial documents should be scanned and transmitted via the bank's trade-services portal, and original transport documents (B/L, AWB) are required for documentary collections.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD foreign-exchange forwards (FXA) entered with licensed Spanish credit institutions under a standard ISDA or local master foreign-exchange agreement

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) against emerging-market currencies such as Latin American local currencies are permissible where a Spanish bank is able to book them via an offshore FX desk or a local subsidiary, but with EMIR reporting and prudent collateral arrangements if used for hedge accounting

Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps / swap contracts) for managing intercompany debt and converting capital-account loans between USD and EUR, provided the transactions are conducted through a regulated counterparty and documented under a proper CSA for margining
European-style EUR/USD FX options and collar strategies used solely for treasury hedging of actual trade receivables and payables, with MiFID II suitability checks by the counterparty bank

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Art. 29.1 Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades, LIS); reduced 15% rate for newly created SLs in the first two tax periods with positive tax base (Art. 29.1 LIS, subject to economic-activity and anti-shell conditions)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For SMEs (INCN < EUR 10M): capitalization reserve (10% reduction of tax base via 10% reserve on equity increase, Art. 25 LIS), leveling reserve (10% reduction up to EUR 1M, five-year reversal, Art. 105 LIS), free 12-month depreciation of new assets (Art. 103 LIS); R&D&I credits: 25% R&D (42% on excess over 2-year average) and 12% technological innovation (Art. 35 LIS); new-entity 15% rate; no digital services tax threshold impact for INCN < EUR 3M in Spain.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite since 2015 (Art. 26 LIS); annual offset capped at 70% of taxable income for entities with INCN < EUR 20M (60% for INCN >= 20M; 50% for INCN >= 60M); no carryback.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades annual self-assessment); filed electronically via AEAT Sede Electrónica (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es) with electronic certificate (DNIe/FNMT/Cl@ve PIN); small entities may use the Renta Sociedades Web assisted filing service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax year-end (Art. 124 LIS). Calendar-year SL: 1-25 July of the following year; non-calendar fiscal years: six months plus 25 days from the closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resultado contable del ejercicio (accounting profit/loss before tax per the statutory financial statements approved for the fiscal year).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders have no entry; the SL's management must reconcile this result with the audited accounts; no consolidation allowed for single-entity SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent differences: adjustments that never reverse (non-deductible expenses, non-taxable income), e.g., penalties, donations without title, over-valuation of stock.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure cross-border payments (royalties, interest) are backed by substance to avoid permanent add-backs; undocumented payments to foreign affiliates are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Temporary differences originating and reversing (e.g., depreciation differences, provisions, IFRS-to-tax adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest limitation (Art. 16.5 LIS: deductible net interest capped at 30% EBITDA, EUR 1M de minimis floor) must be tracked here for shareholder loans from non-resident parents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compensation of prior-year tax loss carryforwards (offset limited to 70% of current taxable income; for entities with INCN < EUR 20M).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses realised before a non-resident shareholding change may be limited if the company structure changed without valid economic reasons (Art. 26.4 LIS).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base imponible del período (taxable base after adjustments and loss compensation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable base is computed at entity level in Spain; non-resident shareholders cannot consolidate losses of the Spanish SL into their home group via this model.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tipo de gravamen aplicable: 25% general, or 15% for a newly created SL in its first two profitable years, plus any applicable co-ownership/cooperative rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced 15% new-entity rate is denied if the SL is a holding/passive entity or was created to house an existing economic activity that had ceased.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bonificaciones y deducciones: double taxation relief, R&D credits, European/international economic double taxation, job creation deductions, plus 10% capitalization reserve and 10% leveling reserve for SMEs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source dividends received by the SL from non-resident subsidiaries may benefit from the participation exemption (Art. 21 LIS) if category requirements are met; a minimal 5% holding one-year holding rule applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Retenciones e ingresos a cuenta: 19% withholdings on interest, dividends, rental income and other Spanish-source income received by the SL during the year (Modelo 193 informative).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholdings borne by the SL are creditable; withholdings imposed on Spanish payments to non-residents are settled by the SL as payer via Modelo 216, not in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cuota diferencial: total liquid (nett) tax payable or refundable, after offsetting payments on account (Modelo 202 instalments) and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A balance refundable may be suspended where the SL has amounts outstanding from earlier periods; payments to non-resident shareholders in anticipation of liquidation are audited.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late self-assessment without prior demand (Art. 27 LGT): recargo 5% (<=3 months), 10% (3-6), 15% (6-12), 20% + late-payment interest (>12 months). Underpaid tax after demand (Art. 191 LGT): proportional penalty 50%-150% of the unduly unpaid amount (reduced to 50% if voluntary before notification, 65% after). Non-submission after notification: 50% plus enforcement surcharge 10%/20% (apremio). Interest of 3.75% notional? actually 'interés de demora' is approx 4.06%? I should not be specific; just 'statutory late-payment interest'.
